contentHtml:
Top mobile app development companies in Hyderabad: the short answer

In short: On GoodFirms' Hyderabad list, as I read it on 16 November 2026, nine firms have ten or more verified reviews. After checking each one's own website for a Hyderabad address and for apps you can install, eight remain: Tvisha Technologies, ZipNom Technologies, iPrism Technologies, Byteridge, Ahex Technologies, Eqaim Technology, Divami Design Labs and Galaxy Tech Solutions, in order of review count. Use them as a starting shortlist, not a verdict.

One thing to say plainly before anything else: this list is written by ElevateBox, a Hyderabad company that builds apps. Every firm below is a competitor of ours. That is why I did not pick them by opinion. I used public signals anyone can check, wrote down the method, and kept ElevateBox out of the ranking. Where we fit is covered in its own short section further down.

This guide was checked in November 2026, against GoodFirms' Hyderabad mobile app development directory, each company's own website, Google Play listings and public company records. Directories re-rank firms often, so expect the order to move.

How I picked and ordered the list

Most "top companies" lists do not say how they were made. Here is exactly what I did, so you can repeat it or disagree with it.

  1. Start from a public directory. I used GoodFirms' Hyderabad mobile app development list, which said it had reviewed 399 firms in the city as of November 2026.
  2. Sort by evidence, not placement. The default view is sorted by "Sponsored". I switched to the Most Reviews sort instead.
  3. Set a floor. I kept firms with at least ten verified reviews. Below that, one or two reviews can swing a rating from 4.6 to 5.0. Nine firms cleared the floor.
  4. Check the company's own site. For each, I looked for a Hyderabad office address and for apps on Google Play or the App Store linked from their own pages.
  5. Check registration where I could. Where a Corporate Identity Number (CIN) was published, I read the incorporation year from it.
  6. Order by review count. Firms tied on review count keep GoodFirms' own order.

One firm fell out at step four. OpenXcell has the most reviews on the Hyderabad page (76), but its own contact page lists offices in Ahmedabad and Las Vegas only. I could not find a Hyderabad address, so I left it out of a Hyderabad list. That is not a judgement on its work.

Source: GoodFirms Hyderabad list, Most Reviews and Tvisha contact page and ZipNom and iPrism portfolio and Eqaim and Galaxy Tech contact page and Qorpiq company record for Ahex and Tofler company record for Divami, read 16 November 2026.

"Not found" means I did not find it on the pages I read, not that it does not exist. Several sites blocked or broke my reader on their contact pages. If a firm makes your shortlist, ask them for the missing item directly.

The eight companies, one by one

These notes stick to what each company publishes and what GoodFirms shows. I have not worked with any of them, and I have left out claims I could not check, such as client counts and team sizes stated in marketing copy.

1. Tvisha Technologies

GoodFirms shows 47 reviews at 4.8 and a founding year of 2003. Its contact page lists Tvisha Technologies Pvt Ltd at Kavuri Hills, Madhapur, plus an office in New Jersey. The homepage links to its own team chat product, Troop Messenger, on both stores. On Google Play the developer is shown as TVISHA, last updated on 5 November 2026, with 10K+ downloads. An app the company publishes itself is a useful signal: you can install it and judge the build quality.

2. ZipNom Technologies

31 reviews at 5.0. GoodFirms says founded 2022, but the CIN printed on its own website (U62091TS2025PTC197974) carries 2025 as the incorporation year. The two can both be true: a team can trade before it incorporates. It is still a question worth asking. Its address is in Banjara Hills. I found no store links on the homepage, so ask for apps you can install.

3. iPrism Technologies

19 reviews at 5.0, founded 2014 per GoodFirms. Its portfolio page is the most checkable of the eight: seven apps with Google Play links, several with App Store links too, including FoodSafari, Medrayder, Kaam Hai Na and Yocto. When I opened FoodSafari on Google Play, the developer shown was Jamir Digital Business Services (OPC) Private Ltd., not iPrism. That is normal and good practice: a client's app should sit in the client's own developer account. It also means the store page alone cannot prove who built it, so call that client.

4. Byteridge

14 reviews at 4.9, founded 2008 per GoodFirms. Its homepage leads with case studies rather than store links, naming work for Microsoft (the Ruuh chatbot), ADP and Deltek. That reads as a firm oriented to larger and international clients. I could not find a street address on the pages I read; ask for one.

5. Ahex Technologies

13 reviews at 4.9. Its homepage says it was founded in July 2009, and GoodFirms agrees. The company record on Qorpiq gives a CIN of U72200TG2012PTC081053, which shows 2012 as the year the private limited company was registered. Again, both can be true; the business may predate the company. The homepage shows case studies rather than store links and describes AI, web, mobile and Odoo ERP work.

6. Eqaim Technology and Services

11 reviews at 5.0, founded 2022 per GoodFirms. Its homepage gives an address at HUDA Techno Enclave, Hyderabad 500081, and three case studies (Young Studios, Prime Lab and Halo). No store links on the homepage.

7. Divami Design Labs

11 reviews at 4.7, founded 2008. The Tofler record gives CIN U72200TG2008PTC062302, which matches 2008. Its site describes design, AI and engineering working together, so expect a design-led studio. Its GoodFirms rate band is $50 to $99 an hour, higher than most of this list, which is consistent with that positioning.

8. Galaxy Tech Solutions

11 reviews at 4.6, founded 2019 per GoodFirms. Its GoodFirms profile says it is a unit of Geeky Digital Solutions Private Limited, registered in Bengaluru. Its contact page lists a Madhapur office, plus Bengaluru, Nellore and Dubai. The legal name on your contract will be Geeky Digital Solutions, not Galaxy Tech Solutions, so check that name in public records.

Where ElevateBox fits

ElevateBox builds apps, websites, WhatsApp and AI automations from Hyderabad. We are not in the GoodFirms review-count list above, so we are not ranked in it, and I would not ask you to take our word over the method. What I can tell you is how we work: code, cloud and credentials stay in the client's name, and a project starts with a ₹3,500 requirement analysis, a call with the people who will build it that ends in a written fixed quotation and timeline before any build starts (how it works). Hold us to the same checks below.

How to shortlist: step by step

A list like this is the start of the work. This is the order I would use to get from eight names to one contract.

Step 1. Write a one-page brief. Who will use the app, the five things it must do, what it connects to (payments, your billing software, WhatsApp), and your deadline. Without it, every quote prices a different app. Our guide to mobile app development cost in India lists what moves the price.

Step 2. Pick three firms whose public work looks like your app. A firm with live food-ordering apps will estimate a food-ordering app better than one with only enterprise case studies, and the reverse is also true.

Step 3. Install their apps. Use them for ten minutes each. Read the latest reviews and the "Updated on" date. An app last updated two years ago tells you something about the maintenance relationship.

Step 4. Confirm the legal entity. Ask for the CIN and GSTIN, and check that the name matches the name on the quote. With Galaxy Tech Solutions, for example, the company is Geeky Digital Solutions Private Limited.

Step 5. Call two past clients. Choose clients whose apps you installed. Ask what went wrong and how the firm handled it. Every project has a bad week.

Step 6. Meet the people who will build it. Not only the sales lead. Ask the developer what they would build first and what they think is risky.

Step 7. Compare written quotes on the same brief. Line by line: screens, integrations, testing, admin panel, store submission, and support after launch. Then read the contract for who owns the code and the store accounts.

For the full verification routine, including the government portals, see our guide on choosing a development partner.

Three worked examples

These businesses are illustrative, not clients. Each shows how the same list leads to a different shortlist.

A clinic chain with a booking app

A three-branch clinic in Kukatpally wants patients to book slots, get reminders and download reports. Health data raises the stakes, so I would put security questions first: where data is stored, who at the firm can see it, how access ends when a developer leaves. From the table, I would favour firms with installable consumer apps, so I can see their booking and login flows, and I would ask each for a health or similar data-sensitive project to call.

A D2C brand adding an app to its Shopify store

A clothing brand selling from Hyderabad wants an app for repeat buyers. The work is mostly catalogue, cart, payments and push notifications, and the risk is in the integration with the existing store. I would ask each firm how they have connected an app to an existing e-commerce backend before, and I would test the checkout of any shopping app they show me, start to finish.

A coaching institute moving tests online

An institute in Ameerpet wants timed tests and results for students and parents. The danger is a thousand students logging in at the same minute. I would ask each firm how they load-test, and ask a past education client what happened on the first busy exam day. A firm with large-client case studies, such as Byteridge's, may be worth a call here even without store links.

Ways a top-companies list misleads you

  1. The default order is paid. GoodFirms states that listings marked "Sponsored" pay for premium placement, and the default sort is "Sponsored". On the day I checked, the "Top 10 at Glance" table placed a firm with 0 reviews at number 3. Switch the sort before you read anything into position.
  2. A city filter is not an office. A firm can appear under Hyderabad and have its main office elsewhere, as OpenXcell's own contact page suggests. If you want to meet the team, ask where they sit.
  3. Founding years are self-reported. For two firms, the year in the CIN differed from the year on GoodFirms. Neither is necessarily wrong, but you should know which entity you are contracting with and how long that entity has existed.
  4. Ratings bunch at the top. All eight firms are between 4.6 and 5.0. A 0.2 difference tells you almost nothing. Read the reviews themselves, especially the most recent.
  5. A store listing does not prove who built an app. Client apps should be published under the client's name, so you need the client's word, not just the store page.
  6. Lists like this one have authors with interests. This one included. That is why the method is written down.

Reading a CIN is quick. It is 21 characters: listed or unlisted status, an industry code, the state code, the year of incorporation, the company type and a registration number (IIFL explainer). In U72200TG2008PTC062302, TG is the state code and 2008 is the year.

A one-hour shortlisting routine

For each firm on your shortlist, I would block about twenty minutes and do this in order:

  1. Open the GoodFirms profile and read the five most recent reviews in full. Note one reviewer to contact. (5 minutes)
  2. Find the CIN and GSTIN on the website, quote or invoice, and check the legal name. (5 minutes)
  3. Install two apps they built and note the developer name and last update date on the store. (7 minutes)
  4. Write down three questions for the call: who builds it, what they would build first, and what happens after launch. (3 minutes)

One more check for later: if a firm ever publishes your app under its own developer account, Google Play has a documented process for transferring an app to your account. It is much easier to start in your own account. If you are still deciding whether you need a company at all, our comparison of freelancers and app development companies in Hyderabad covers that choice.
